title: EFT Data, Scales, Wilsonian Action and Finite Matching

items.title: Finite-regulator EFT model and scale data
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use natural units c=ℏ=1, with physical dimensions assigned using the QFT unit convention of the selected model. A finite-regulator effective-field-theory model-data record consists of a finite undirected graph Γ=(X,EΓ) with nonempty vertex set X, retained real coordinates ℓ∈ℝ^X, integrated real coordinates χ∈ℝ^X, a Borel ultraviolet action SUV(ℓ,χ)∈ℝ, and a specified Borel probability measure νH on ℝ^X for the integrated coordinates. Define dΓ(x,y) as the least number of edges in a path from x to y, with dΓ(x,y)=+∞ when no path exists. Equip ℝ^X with the coordinate inner product $u^Tv=\sum_{x\in X}u_xv_x$ and its norm $\|u\|=(u^Tu)^{1/2}$; matrix entries refer to the standard coordinate basis, I is the identity, and $\|A\|=\sup\{\|Au\|:\|u\|=1\}$. The full ultraviolet data are these objects before any integration. This definition does not assert that the integral of exp(−SUV) exists; finiteness and positivity are checked when the Wilsonian action is defined.

For the positive heavy-scalar Gaussian submodel, include a real symmetric matrix $A$ on $\mathbb R^X$ satisfying $u^TAu\ge0$ for every u and $A_{xy}=0$ when $d_\Gamma(x,y)>1$. Its entries have mass-squared units and its operator norm satisfies $\sqrt{\lVert A\rVert}\le\Lambda$. Choose $M>0$ and put $K=M^2I+A$; for $u\ne0$, $u^TKu\ge M^2\lVert u\rVert^2>0$. Require νH to be the centered Gaussian probability with covariance $K^{-1}$: after a fixed ordering of X, it is $N_{|X|}(0,K^{-1})$, meaning every real linear projection $u^T\chi$ has normal law with mean zero and variance $u^TK^{-1}u$. This optional law uses the Axiom of Choice under the multivariate-normal supplier's convention; no Gaussian law is required of the general model record. The heavy coordinate χ has mass-inverse units, so $\chi^TK\chi$ is dimensionless. Specify a Borel source map $J:\mathbb R^X\to\mathbb R^X$ whose values have mass units, so $J(\ell)^T\chi$ is dimensionless. Complexify to $\mathbb C^X$ with first-variable-linear Hermitian pairing $\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{x\in X}z_x\overline{w_x}$ and $A_{\mathbb C}(x+iy)=Ax+iAy$. Real symmetry and positivity make $A_{\mathbb C}$ self-adjoint and nonnegative. Assume countable choice for the spectral supplier in the QFT unit convention and use its normalized projection-valued measure $E_{A_{\mathbb C}}$: Borel sets map to orthogonal projections, the total value is I, and countable additivity holds on each vector. Define $P_E$ as $E_{A_{\mathbb C}}([0,E^2])$ restricted to ℝ^X, equivalently the real orthogonal projection onto the sum of A-eigenspaces with eigenvalues in $[0,E^2]$; the real symmetric matrix's eigenspaces make this restriction real. When the source is restricted to external energy E, require $J(\ell)=P_EJ(\ell)$ for every ℓ.

The scale data are a positive Wilsonian matching scale $\mu_W$, a heavy mass $M>0$, an external energy bound $E\ge0$, and a regulator cutoff $\Lambda>0$, with $\sqrt{\|A\|}\le\Lambda$ in the Gaussian submodel. The Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$ records where the retained low-coordinate action is specified; $M$ is the heavy quadratic mass; $E$ bounds the admitted source spectrum; and $\Lambda$ bounds the finite regulator. These are separately named parameters, and this definition imposes no relation among their numerical values. A small-remainder theorem may require an additional hierarchy such as $E<M$.

Light and heavy name the roles in the declared split: ℓ is retained at μW and χ is integrated in the finite measure νH. They do not assert that every retained field is massless or that every integrated field is heavy in an unrestricted continuum theory. If the model includes non-Abelian gauge data, record the actual global group, Lie algebra, principal bundle, representations, and admitted bundle sectors as one supplied gauge-data object. That object selects no connection, action, or quantum measure by itself. The Gaussian submodel below keeps any such gauge data as fixed context and makes no gauge-field integration claim.

This is a finite-dimensional regulator description. It makes no assertion that a general interacting functional measure exists, that a cutoff can be removed, or that any selected model describes nature.

items.title: Finite-regulator Wilsonian action
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Take a finite-regulator model datum with retained coordinates $\ell$, integrated coordinates $h$, a normalized Borel probability measure $\nu_H$ on the finite-dimensional $h$-space, and a real Borel ultraviolet action $S_{\rm UV}(\ell,h)$. For each retained configuration $\ell$ define

$$
Z_H(\ell):=\int e^{-S_{\rm UV}(\ell,h)}\,d\nu_H(h).
$$

On the domain of $\ell$ for which $0<Z_H(\ell)<\infty$, the finite-regulator Wilsonian action at scale $\mu_W$ is

$$
S_W(\ell;\mu_W):=-\log Z_H(\ell).
$$

Thus “integrating out” the high sector means this specified finite integral over $h$ while $\ell$ is held fixed. The measure, action, regulator, and low/high split are inputs; the definition does not assert that every interacting model has a finite or well-defined integral. Replacing $\nu_H$ by a positive constant multiple changes $S_W$ only by an additive constant independent of $\ell$, which is fixed by the chosen normalization convention.

For comparison, fix the following finite Euclidean convention for a one-particle-irreducible (1PI) effective action. Separately supply a Borel probability $\rho$ on the retained space $\mathbb R^X$, and pair a source $j\in(\mathbb R^X)^*$ with $\ell\in\mathbb R^X$ by $j\cdot\ell=\sum_{x\in X}j_x\ell_x$, with source units chosen to make the pairing dimensionless. On a nonempty open set $U\subset(\mathbb R^X)^*$ require $0<\int e^{j\cdot\ell}\,d\rho(\ell)<\infty$ and define the connected source-generating function $W(j)=\log\int e^{j\cdot\ell}\,d\rho(\ell)$. Require $W$ to be $C^2$ on $U$ and its gradient $\nabla W:U\to V$ to be a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto an open set $V\subset\mathbb R^X$ (a bijection with continuously differentiable map and inverse). For $\varphi\in V$ set $j(\varphi)=(\nabla W)^{-1}(\varphi)$ and define the Legendre transform $\Gamma(\varphi)=j(\varphi)\cdot\varphi-W(j(\varphi))$. This defines the finite Euclidean 1PI action on $V$ under these additional hypotheses; no graph expansion or existence of these additional data is asserted. It is a different construction from the high-coordinate integral above, which needs none of $\rho,U,V,W,\Gamma$.

items.title: Finite-regulator derivative expansion and truncation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
For the finite undirected graph $\Gamma=(X,E_\Gamma)$, define $d_\Gamma(x,y)$ as the least number of edges in a path from $x$ to $y$, and set $d_\Gamma(x,y)=+\infty$ if no path exists. Concatenating paths gives the triangle inequality for this extended distance. Identify $\mathbb R^X$ with real coordinate vectors indexed by $X$; for a matrix $B$ on this space, $B_{xy}$ denotes its row-$x$, column-$y$ entry in the standard coordinate basis. For an integer $r\ge0$, say that $B$ has range at most $r$ when $B_{xy}=0$ whenever $d_\Gamma(x,y)>r$. The positive heavy-sector matrix $A$ from the model data has range at most one. A derivative expansion of its inverse kernel is the formal operator series

$$
(M^2I+A)^{-1}\sim M^{-2}\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}(-A/M^2)^r.
$$

Its order-$N$ truncation, for an integer $N\ge0$, is the finite operator

$$
S_N:=M^{-2}\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-A/M^2)^r.
$$

It has range at most $N$ in this regulator. For a source $J$ supported in the spectral interval $[0,E^2]$ of $A$, the dimensionless power-counting parameter is $E/M$. This definition is an organized finite-order approximation; it does not assert convergence for unrestricted sources, a generic error bound, or a continuum local-operator expansion. Under the Axiom of Choice and the positive heavy-mode Gaussian matching-data hypotheses, the low-momentum matching remainder theorem gives, for $J=P_EJ$ and $K=M^2I+A$, the conditional bound $\|K^{-1}J-S_NJ\|\le M^{-2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}\|J\|$. In this finite real symmetric positive-semidefinite setting the theorem applies on the complexification with its coordinate Hermitian inner product and restricts to real sources. This bound is useful when $E<M$; it asserts no generic interacting-action remainder.

items.title: Successive finite Gaussian shells compose
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; local A-page mathematical supplier required for the finite shell composition; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, let $C_1,C_2$ be real symmetric positive-semidefinite $d\times d$ covariance matrices, and let $f:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty]$ be Borel. For a covariance matrix $C$, let $\gamma_C$ denote the centered Gaussian probability with covariance $C$, including when $C$ is singular, and define

$$
T_Cf(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x+z)\,d\gamma_C(z).
$$

For a finite nonnegative Borel potential $V$, $0<T_C(e^{-V})(x)\le1$; define the finite nonnegative potential $V_C(x):=-\log T_C(e^{-V})(x)$. Then

$$
T_{C_2}(T_{C_1}f)(x)=T_{C_1+C_2}f(x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^d)
$$

as an equality in $[0,\infty]$, and

$$
e^{-(V_{C_1})_{C_2}(x)}=e^{-V_{C_1+C_2}(x)}.
$$

The Gaussian measures are normalized probabilities, so no determinant or vacuum constant appears. This is a finite-regulator composition identity; it asserts no derivative equation along a covariance path and no continuum limit.

items.title: Finite heavy-scalar Gaussian matching
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, equip $\mathbb R^d$ with inner product $u^Tv$ and norm $\|u\|=(u^Tu)^{1/2}$, let $A$ be a real symmetric positive-semidefinite $d\times d$ matrix, let $M>0$, and put $K=M^2I+A$, where $I$ is the identity on $\mathbb R^d$. Then $K$ is positive definite. Use natural units with $\chi$ in mass-inverse units, $A$ and $K$ in mass-squared units, and a source $J\in\mathbb R^d$ in mass units. Let $E\ge0$. Define $\mathbb C^d=\mathbb R^d+i\mathbb R^d$ with Hermitian inner product $\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k=1}^d z_k\overline{w_k}$ and the complex-linear map $A_{\mathbb C}(x+iy)=Ax+iAy$. Real symmetry and nonnegativity make $A_{\mathbb C}$ self-adjoint and nonnegative; use its normalized spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_{\mathbb C}}$, whose Borel-set values are orthogonal projections, whose total value is the identity, and which is strongly countably additive, as in the positive heavy-mode Gaussian matching-data definition. Set $P_E:=E_{A_{\mathbb C}}([0,E^2])$, restricted to $\mathbb R^d$, and assume $J=P_EJ$. Thus $J$ lies in the sum of the eigenspaces of $A$ with eigenvalues in $[0,E^2]$. Let $\gamma_{K^{-1}}=N_d(0,K^{-1})$ be the centered normalized Gaussian law whose every linear projection $u^T\chi$ is normal with mean zero and variance $u^TK^{-1}u$, and define

$$ Z_H(J):=\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{J^T\chi}\,d\gamma_{K^{-1}}(\chi) $$

$$ \Delta S_W(J):=-\log Z_H(J) $$

For each integer $N\ge0$, put

$$
S_NJ:=M^{-2}\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-A/M^2)^rJ.
$$

Then the finite Gaussian expectation $Z_H(J)$ is finite and positive, and

$$ Z_H(J)=\exp\!\left(\tfrac12J^TK^{-1}J\right) $$

$$ \Delta S_W(J)=-\tfrac12J^TK^{-1}J $$

The inverse-kernel and action remainders satisfy

$$
\|K^{-1}J-S_NJ\|\le M^{-2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}\|J\|,
$$

$$ \left|\Delta S_W(J)+\tfrac12J^TS_NJ\right| \le \frac{\|J\|^2}{2M^2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1} $$

These are exact conditional statements for a finite positive quadratic heavy sector. The remainder is small in the stated band when $E<M$; no claim is made for unrestricted sources, arbitrary interactions, a continuum measure, or a differentiated Wilsonian flow.

items.title: One-dimensional finite Gaussian matching and shell composition
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned B-page worked example; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume AC. Use one positive mass unit $m_0$ and a one-site finite regulator with $M=2m_0$, $A=(m_0^2)$, $E=m_0$, $\mu_W=\tfrac32m_0$, $\Lambda=3m_0$, source $J=(m_0)$, and truncation order $N=0$. Then $K=M^2I+A=(5m_0^2)$. Let $\gamma_{K^{-1}}=N_1(0,K^{-1})$ be the centered normalized Gaussian with covariance $K^{-1}$. For $Z_H(J)=\int e^{J^T\chi}\,d\gamma_{K^{-1}}(\chi)$ and the action increment $\Delta S_W=-\log Z_H(J)$, the exact increment is $-1/10$, the order-zero approximation is $-1/8$, the vector remainder is $1/(20m_0)$, and the action remainder is $1/40\le1/32$.

For a separate dimensionless shell coordinate, let $\gamma_C=N_1(0,C)$ be the centered normalized Gaussian of variance $C$, define $T_Cf(x)=\int f(x+z)\,d\gamma_C(z)$, and take $f(x)=x^2$, $C_1=1$, and $C_2=3$. The successive normalized shell value at zero and the combined-shell value are both $4$.

This is a model-specific finite calculation. It reports no observation and asserts no continuum limit or general interacting matching rule.
items.physical_scope: A one-coordinate finite Gaussian regulator example and a separate normalized shell calculation; no empirical claim, continuum limit, or generic matching theorem.
